data.narrative:
SiPearl is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Philippe Notton that has raised €130M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 12 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors (including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor) and 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method here. Using total capital raised of €130M as a proxy for Series A valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of progression to the next stage yields an implied valuation of €260M. This represents the core quantitative anchor given constraints on comparable data.

Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied without SiPearl's revenue, which is not disclosed. The public semiconductor sector trades at a median P/S of 21.5x, but revenue data for the target is unavailable. A narrow peer-multiple approach also cannot be executed; while 12 same-sector private companies exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers yields fewer than three datapoints—insufficient for robust median derivation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €221M–€299M, with a median point of €260M. Key uncertainties center on revenue trajectory and the absence of granular financial disclosure typical of early-stage private semiconductor companies, limiting validation through conventional multiple-based methods. Stage-progression provides the sole defensible quantitative signal at this juncture.
